Your computer has a virtual display of its own: an X server (Xvnc) with a VNC view a person can open, 1024x768. Nobody else is using it, so it is the place to open and drive GUI apps. Apps you start -- with clawtilla_display_launch, or any command you run through clawtilla_computer_exec -- appear there. Look at it with clawtilla_display_screenshot and act on it with clawtilla_display_click, clawtilla_display_type, clawtilla_display_key and clawtilla_display_scroll; coordinates are the screen's own pixels, from the top left. clawtilla_display_windows lists what is open. Your commands still run on the real machine clawtilla is on, under the same confinement as any host command. A person can watch this screen and take it; while they hold it your clicks and keys are refused, and you should wait for them to give it back. A person watching may also have it open in a VNC viewer.
